question: Are there any red flags in Apple's financial statements?

answer.summary: Apple's FY2023 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2023) carries several pre-computed red flags, although the auditor issued an unqualified opinion dated November 2, 2023 [T00627]. Operating cash flow fell 9.5% to $110.54B and free cash flow fell 10.6% to $99.58B, while capex rose 2.3% to $10.96B [F00224][F01389][F00236]. Liquidity is a medium-risk flag: the current ratio was below 1 in both FY2022 (0.88) and FY2023 (0.99) [F01420][F01421]. Inventory grew 28% in FY2023 while cost of revenue fell 4%, flagged as a collection/build-up risk [F00099][F00022]. Revenue fell 2.8% to $383.29B and operating income fell 4.3% to $114.30B, and interest coverage dropped 29% to 29.1x [F00013][F00037][F01432]. Shareholder payouts of $92.58B consumed 93% of free cash flow in FY2023, leaving little room to absorb a downturn [F01448][F01389].

key_numbers.metric: Inventory growth vs cost of revenue
Dividends + buybacks as % of free cash flow

drivers: FY2023 free cash flow decline (-10.6%, $111.44B -> $99.58B) coincides with the 9.5% operating cash flow decline ($122.15B -> $110.54B); capex was roughly flat (+2.3%), so the cash-flow deterioration is on the operating side rather than investment [F01389][F00224][F00236].
Inventory build-up is the medium-risk driver: FY2023 inventory grew 28% while cost of revenue fell 4%, a divergence the screen flags as collection/build-up risk [F00099][F00022].

Shareholder payout is a low-risk but binding constraint: dividends+buybacks of $92.58B were 93% of FY2023 free cash flow (94% in FY2022 at $104.24B of $111.44B), leaving little buffer in a downturn [F01448][F01447][F01389][F01388].
Liquidity improved but remains flagged: current ratio rose from 0.88 (FY2022) to 0.99 (FY2023), still below 1.0 in both years [F01420][F01421].
risks_and_red_flags: Inventory vs cost of sales: FY2023 inventory grew 28% while cost of revenue fell 4% (collection/build-up risk) [F00099][F00022].
Operating cash flow decline: FY2023 OCF fell 9.5% ($122.15B -> $110.54B) [F00224].
Shareholder payout vs free cash flow: FY2022 dividends+buybacks ($104.24B) were 94% of FCF ($111.44B) [F01447][F01388].
Shareholder payout vs free cash flow: FY2023 dividends+buybacks ($92.58B) were 93% of FCF ($99.58B) [F01448][F01389].
Operating income decline: FY2023 operating income fell 4.3% ($119.44B -> $114.30B) [F00037].
Interest coverage drop: FY2023 interest coverage fell 29% (40.7x -> 29.1x) [F01432].
data_quality_notes: 3 accounting identities passed, 0 failed for the screened numbers; no text-vs-table conflicts were reported.
Free cash flow is a derived metric (CFO - capex) per the evidence view; operating cash flow and capex are XBRL-tagged [F00224][F00236][F01389].
The current-ratio, payout-ratio and interest-coverage items are pre-computed screen outputs, not separately re-derived here.
Audit opinion was unqualified (PCAOB standards), report dated November 2, 2023 [T00627].

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 actuals show broad-based declines: revenue -2.8%, operating income -4.3%, operating cash flow -9.5%, free cash flow -10.6%, and interest coverage -29%, with the current ratio still below 1.0; the two-year FCF/OCF trend is characterized as 'stable (weak)' [F00013][F00037][F00224][F01389][F01432][F01421].
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: Not in the retrieved evidence - no management guidance figures were provided in the narrative evidence.

follow_up_checks: Inventory composition (finished goods vs components/raw materials) to determine whether the 28% FY2023 build is deliberate supply-chain positioning or demand softness [F00099].
Current-ratio trajectory and short-term debt/commercial paper levels in FY2024 filings, given sub-1.0 ratios in FY2022 and FY2023 [F01420][F01421].
Whether operating cash flow recovers in FY2024 quarterly filings after the 9.5% FY2023 decline [F00224].
Sustainability of the ~93% payout ratio versus free cash flow and remaining buyback authorization [F01448][F01389].
Drivers of the interest-coverage drop (interest expense versus operating income) behind the move from 40.7x to 29.1x [F01432].
